title: Zelenskyy Praises Trump for Signing Sweeping Russia Sanctions Bill
snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked President Donald Trump after he signed a bipartisan bill expanding sanctions and tariffs against Moscow.
content:
WASHINGTON — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy offered swift praise to President Donald Trump on Friday after the White House signed into law a sweeping, bipartisan bill aimed at choking off Russia's economic lifelines as the war in Ukraine enters its fifth year.

The legislation, championed by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham before his sudden passing, expands both primary and secondary sanctions on Moscow. It targets Russian political leaders, oligarchs, banking institutions, and the clandestine 'shadow fleet' of oil tankers used by the Kremlin to bypass international energy limits. Additionally, the measure extends key sanctions on Iran's energy and defense sectors while authorizing targeted tariffs on top buyers of Russian oil and gas.

A Tribute to Lindsey Graham

In a message posted to Telegram late Friday, Zelenskyy called the law 'critically important' and expressed gratitude to Trump and lawmakers across Capitol Hill. He framed the bill's passage as a fitting tribute to Sen. Graham, a staunch defender of U.S. aid to Kyiv who died recently from an aortic tear.

'When Lindsey Graham was here in Ukraine, he would always talk about how important it was not to ease pressure on Russia, to strengthen sanctions and seek a path to peace,' Zelenskyy wrote, calling for rapid enforcement of the new measures. 'Peace comes through strength. Calm comes through security. And the best guarantee of security is resolve.'

Kremlin Pushback and Capitol Hill Divide

The reaction from Moscow was sharply hostile. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov warned that new American sanctions would 'definitely complicate efforts to find a peaceful settlement.' Meanwhile, former Russian President Dmitry Medvedev lashed out on social media, dismissing the legislation as 'Russophobic' and insulting the late South Carolina senator.

On Capitol Hill, the bill cleared the Senate easily in an 86-11 vote, but faced a more divided House, passing 262 to 159. While 58 Democrats supported the measure, the majority voted against it alongside seven Republicans. House Democratic leaders, including Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, cited concerns over granting broad discretionary authority to the executive branch.
